articles.title_orig: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.title_zh: Obama judge halts Trump firing bid as decades-old legal authority tees up possible major reversal
articles.content_orig:
U.S. District Court Judge James Boasberg, who blocked President Donald Trump from deporting hundreds of Venezuelan migrants, is among the judges who have attracted attention from critics. 'Fox News @ Night' takes a closer look.
An Obama-appointed judge blocked President Donald Trump from firing court-appointed U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington Roger Rogoff, ordering the Justice Department to recognize Rogoff as the rightful officeholder and restore his ability to serve.
"This is yet another ruling from an activist judge trying to thwart President Trump’s agenda and undermine his constitutional authority. U.S. attorneys serve at the pleasure of the President," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.
Judge Stanley Bastian, who was first nominated by Obama in 2013, issued a preliminary injunction reinstating Rogoff and barring the administration from treating him as having been lawfully removed. The ruling sets up a legal fight over whether a president can fire a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges. A 1979 Justice Department opinion and a 2000 federal appeals court ruling both concluded that the president has that authority.
"We disagree with the decision and intend to seek an immediate stay and will appeal," the DOJ Rapid Response account wrote.
TRUMP ADMIN FIRES US ATTORNEY IN SEATTLE MINUTES AFTER HE WAS APPOINTED
President Donald Trump’s administration secured an interim Supreme Court victory allowing it to continue third-country deportations while the legal battle plays out. (Getty Images)
Some legal experts and conservative attorneys took to social media to sharply criticize the ruling, arguing it infringes on the president's constitutional authority over the executive branch.
"Another lawless and dangerous ruling. Violating the separation of powers. By another Democrat activist judge. This time? Seattle Obama Judge Stanley Bastian," wrote Article III founder and president Mike Davis .
"Democrat judges handpicked their own U.S. attorney. The President, through his attorney general, fired him. Under Article II of the Constitution , the President clearly has the executive power to fire Justice Department officials," Davis added.
Davis also noted Bastian’s first name was misspelled in the order, missing the "e" in Stanley.
'ROGUE' OBAMA JUDGE'S SMACKDOWN OF TRUMP ELECTION RULES PROVOKES OMINOUS WARNING FROM WHITE HOUSE DEPUTY
FILE - The majority of the cuts were aimed at Health and Human Services programs. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)
"The Federal Judge misspelled his own name in his order. That's how you know it's quality legal work," wrote one user.
"Now Judge Bastian created an unnecessary constitutional crisis by essentially ordering a coup at the Justice Department, by ordering the removal of the President’s pick and putting in Bastian’s judicial puppet. The Ninth Circuit must fix this. Or the Supreme Court will have to step in. Again," Davis concluded.
"The President's power to remove U.S. Attorneys must be unfettered consistent with Article II of the Constitution. Judge Stanley Bastian is wrong here to order Rogoff reinstated. I predict Judge Bastian will eventually be reversed, whether at the Ninth Circuit or by the Supreme Court," said Oversight Project litigation vice president Jeff Clark .
WHITE HOUSE RIPS ‘ACTIVIST’ BIDEN JUDGE WHO UPENDED TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP ORDER
Justice Department lawyers asked a federal judge Friday to dismiss a lawsuit challenging the Anti-Weaponization Fund, arguing Attorney General Todd Blanche formally terminated it Aug. 2. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
"Judicial overreach, plain and simple. The judiciary does not get to run the Executive Branch. Period," said Holtzman Vogel partner Brian Nieves .
In Myers v. United States (1926), which centered on President Woodrow Wilson's firing of a postmaster without Senate consent, the Supreme Court ruled that the president generally has constitutional authority to remove executive branch officers.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
More recently, the Justice Department’s Office of Legal Counsel concluded in a 1979 opinion that the president’s statutory authority to remove "each United States attorney" also extends to prosecutors appointed by federal judges.
The case is the latest in a string of legal fights over President Trump's U.S. attorney appointments, following similar disputes in New Jersey, Virginia and New York.
A similar dispute unfolded in New Jersey after the administration sought to keep Alina Habba leading the U.S. attorney’s office after her interim term ended. Federal courts ultimately rejected the administration’s effort to maintain her authority, although the judges’ original appointee, Desiree Grace, did not simply take over the office.
Rogoff’s case goes a step further, directly testing whether a president can remove a U.S. attorney appointed by federal judges under the statutory process for filling a vacancy.

articles.title_orig: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.title_zh: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.content_orig:
Long-term data reinforce durable efficacy and safety of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in late-onset Pompe disease
BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc . (Nasdaq: BMRN ) today announced new data evaluating the efficacy and safety of POMBILITI® (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + OPFOLDA® (miglustat) in late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) were presented at the 31st Annual Congress of the World Muscle Society (WMS), in Hiroshima, Japan.
These results from the PROPEL open-label extension (OLE) study of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, which were shared in a late-breaking presentation, demonstrated durable motor function outcomes and relative stabilization of pulmonary function over long-term follow-up. The analysis included data from 82 individuals who received POMBILITI + OPFOLDA continuously from baseline observed in the initial PROPEL study (PROPEL baseline) to year five. For the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)-experienced cohort, the mean duration of prior ERT at baseline was 7.6 years. These data represent long-term benefits for people with LOPD followed in the study, including both ERT-experienced and ERT-naïve cohorts.
"These five-year results demonstrate that POMBILITI and OPFOLDA can provide durable, long-term benefits for people living with late-onset Pompe disease, including those who had been on enzyme replacement therapy for years before enrolling in the study," said Greg Friberg, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Research & Development Officer at BioMarin. "Sustaining motor function and limiting pulmonary decline for up to five years in a progressive disease like LOPD is clinically meaningful, and we remain committed to continuing to share long-term evidence to inform the care of people with this rare genetic condition."
Table 1. Efficacy Measures With POMBILITI + OPFOLDA From PROPEL Baseline (BL) for up to Five Years
Mean (standard deviation, SD) change from baseline in % predicted six-minute walk distance (pp6MWD)
Mean (SD) change from baseline in % predicted forced vital capacity (ppFVC)
No new safety signals were identified. 51.2% of participants (n=42) experienced treatment-related adverse events, the majority of which were manageable. Five individuals discontinued treatment for safety reasons, including two due to serious treatment-related adverse events (chills and hypoxia [n=1], anaphylactoid reaction [n=1]).
Phase 1/2 Data Show Positive Dystrophin Expression and Favorable Tolerability With Nivudirsen (BMN 351)
Additional presentations at WMS included data evaluating nivudirsen (BMN 351), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide for ambulatory boys ages 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. Included in these presentations was an update from the ongoing Phase 1/2 351-201 study, which was previously shared at the 19th International Congress on Neuromuscular Diseases in July. Results from 351-201 showed treatment with nivudirsen was generally well tolerated and led to consistently positive outcomes across multiple measures of therapeutic benefit, including expression of near full-length dystrophin.
Below are key presentations at WMS, with all times listed in Japan Standard Time:
Phase 1/2 Results of BMN 351, an Antisense Oligonucleotide for Exon 51 Skip-Amenable Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Poster Presentation #2.66P Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Comprehensive Panel of Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic and Biomarker Measures Drives Clinical Development of BMN 351 for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy E-Poster Presentation #2.43eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Muscle Composition and Muscle Injury Biomarkers Improve With BMN 351 Treatment E-Poster Presentation #2.59eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Five-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline E-Poster Presentation #3.081LBeP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Four-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline Poster Presentation #3.56P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Baseline Disease Burden and Real-World Monitoring Practices: Global Insights From the followME Pompe Journey Registry Poster Presentation #3.57P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
ATB200-03/07 Danish Subpopulation: Four-Year Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease E-Poster Presentation #3.35eP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
About the PROPEL Open-Label Extension Study
The Phase 3 open-label extension (OLE) study (ATB200-07; NCT04138277 ) is a multicenter, international study designed to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in adults with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) who completed the Phase 3 PROPEL study (ATB200-03; NCT03729362 ). Of the 118 people treated in the OLE, 82 continued POMBILITI + OPFOLDA treatment from PROPEL (62 ERT-experienced prior to PROPEL; 20 ERT-naïve) and 37 switched from the comparator arm to POMBILITI + OPFOLDA (29 ERT-experienced; eight ERT-naïve).
The study evaluates long-term changes from PROPEL baseline in six-minute walk distance (6MWD, the primary endpoint in PROPEL), forced vital capacity (FVC), creatine kinase (CK) and hexose tetrasaccharide (Hex4) levels, and patient-reported outcomes, as well as long-term safety.
The 351-201 trial ( NCT06280209 ) is a Phase 1/2 multicenter open-label dose-escalation study evaluating BMN 351 for the treatment of boys aged 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy with a specific genetic change amenable to exon 51 skipping. The primary endpoints examine the safety and tolerability of BMN 351, the secondary endpoints assess plasma, urine and muscle pharmacokinetics, and key exploratory endpoints include exon-skipping efficiency, dystrophin expression, immunogenicity and functional assessments.
The study is being conducted in three cohorts, with Cohort 1 being divided into Cohort 1A and Cohort 1B. In Cohort 1A, three boys received increasing doses once every two weeks with a visit to assess safety measures collected the week after dosing prior to escalating doses of BMN 351. In part two, the participants in Cohort 1A transitioned to once-weekly dosing. The participants in Cohort 1B, 2 and 3 will receive low (6 mg/kg), medium (9 mg/kg) and high (12 mg/kg) doses of BMN 351 and continue once-weekly dosing at that same dose.
For more information, please visit clinicaltrials.biomarin.com .
About Late-Onset Pompe Disease
Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) is an inherited lysosomal disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA). Reduced or absent levels of GAA lead to accumulation of glycogen in cells, which is believed to result in the clinical manifestations of Pompe disease. LOPD can be severe and debilitating with progressive muscle weakness throughout the body that worsens over time, particularly in skeletal muscles and muscles that control breathing.
About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe neuromuscular condition that leads to progressive muscle weakness and premature mortality. DMD is caused by genetic changes that result in the absence or dysfunction of dystrophin, an essential protein that is necessary for preserving muscle function.
As an X-linked disorder, DMD primarily affects young boys, with onset of symptoms occurring around 2 to 3 years of age. The incidence of DMD is up to 1 in 3,600 to 6,000 live male births.
Individuals with DMD experience serious functional impairments, including loss of limb strength and ambulation, and respiratory and cardiovascular impacts that require lifelong care.
POMBILITI + OPFOLDA is a two-component therapy that consists of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga, a bis-M6P-enriched rhGAA that facilitates high-affinity uptake through the M6P receptor while retaining its capacity for processing into the most active form of the enzyme, and the oral enzyme stabilizer

articles.title_orig: When should I get the flu shot? What experts say is the ideal time to protect yourself
articles.title_zh: When should I get the flu shot? What experts say is the ideal time to protect yourself
articles.content_orig:
Should you get your flu shot with a Covid vaccine? Here’s the guidance from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
It’s October and time for flu shots.
Medical experts urge getting a flu vaccination soon, before influenza starts spreading widely — and to get up to date on protection against other fall respiratory viruses, too. Updated COVID-19 shots are available now, plus shots for people especially vulnerable to another winter risk called RSV.
Stream Connecticut News for free, 24/7, wherever you are.
While these infections make many people feel miserable for a few days before they recover, every year flu alone causes hundreds of thousands of hospitalizations in the U.S. and kills tens of thousands.
Vaccination isn’t “a guarantee that we’re going to prevent illness. But just like the seat belt in your car, it decreases risk” of the worst outcomes, said Dr. Ryan Stanton of the American College of Emergency Physicians.
Fall vaccine advice usually comes from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and its independent advisory panel. But this year that panel, which influences state and insurance vaccine policies, is caught in a court battle and the CDC hasn't updated its advice.
Now doctors’ groups are filling the gap: the American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Infectious Diseases Society of America have posted vaccination guidelines for their patient populations plus the scientific evidence behind them.
Just about everybody starting at age 6 months needs flu vaccination, the medical societies agree. But flu is particularly dangerous for people 65 and older, pregnant women, young children and people of any age who have chronic health problems, including asthma, diabetes, heart disease and weak immune systems. The last two flu seasons brought unusually high numbers of child deaths, the vast majority of them in unvaccinated kids.
The vaccines don't block all flu infections, but they do help prevent the worst outcomes, decreasing older adults' hospitalizations by 31% last year, according to the Vaccine Integrity Project, a public health group based at the University of Minnesota.
Three “enhanced” flu vaccines are designed to better protect seniors. The American Academy of Family Physicians urges them to choose one — “but do not delay your vaccination if that one’s not available,” said AAFP’s Dr. Sarah Nosal.
The Food and Drug Administration recently approved a new choice for people ages 50 and older, the first flu vaccine made with the same mRNA technology that was key to ending the COVID-19 pandemic. One study found Moderna's mFlusiva was 27% more effective against symptomatic illness among 50- to 64-year-olds than a standard shot.
The shot-averse could choose a nasal spray, FluMist, if they're ages 2 to 49 and meet other health criteria.
COVID-19 shots once were recommended for just about everyone by federal health agencies, but like last year, the FDA has only formally approved them for higher-risk people — those ages 65 and older or younger people with at least one health condition that increases their risk.
Still, the family physicians recommend all adults get a COVID-19 vaccination, especially seniors and those with other risk factors. Adults 65 and older should get a fall dose and then a second dose six months later, as immunity wanes over time, Nosal said.
The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends a COVID-19 shot for all children ages 6 months to 23 months, and for older kids with high-risk conditions. It also supports vaccination for any child whose parent wishes it.
With millions of shots administered, there’s no evidence that coronavirus vaccination during pregnancy increases the risk of miscarriage or other problems, “so please get the vaccine,” said ACOG’s Dr. Christina Davidson.
Depending on age, people can choose a shot from Moderna, Pfizer, or the only non-mRNA version from Novavax and Sanofi.
Just like with flu vaccines, these shots are better at preventing severe disease than mild cases. The Vaccine Integrity Project said last fall’s COVID-19 shots cut the risk of hospitalization by 53% in seniors and slashed emergency room visits for very young children.
Common side effects for flu and COVID-19 vaccines are mild and temporary, such as sore arms, fatigue, headaches, muscle aches, and mild fever. They occurred somewhat more often with the new mFlusiva than with standard flu shots.
While pediatricians and some clinics offer both flu and coronavirus shots, they're most common in pharmacies.
For COVID-19 shots, states have more pharmacy rules. For example, Walgreens says it offers those shots without a prescription in all but two states, Arizona and Oregon, but can provide doses for children as young as 3 in some states while others have higher age limits.
Medicare covers the fall shots and most private health insurers say they plan to continue doing so through 2027. If you want to choose mFlusiva, the new Moderna flu option, make sure to double check that your insurance covers it.
Flu experts say October is best, although vaccinations will remain available through the fall — just remember it can take two weeks for protection to kick in. COVID-19 cases rose in the late summer and usually do again around the winter holidays. Some experts say it's also OK to time the coronavirus shot a few weeks ahead of an event you wouldn’t want to miss because of illness, like a special trip or get-together.
RSV, or respiratory syncytial virus, typically is a cold-like nuisance during the fall, winter and early spring. But it can be severe, even life-threatening, for infants and older adults.
The family physicians recommend a one-time vaccination for adults 75 and older, people 50 to 74 who are at increased risk, or younger people with weak immune systems.
It’s also recommended during late pregnancy to protect infants born during RSV season. Separately, the pediatricians recommend a vaccine-like medication for those infants whose moms weren't vaccinated and some other high-risk babies.

articles.title_orig: COVID-19 Drops Out of World’s Top 10 Causes of Death for First Time Since Pandemic Began
articles.title_zh: COVID-19 Drops Out of World’s Top 10 Causes of Death for First Time Since Pandemic Began
articles.content_orig:
By GREG WOODFIELD IN UNION CITY, TENNESSEE
Published: 16:26 EDT, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EDT, 2 October 2026
The doctor at the center of the botched execution of murderer and Satanist Christa Pike is exclusively pictured by the Daily Mail at his isolated family home – less than 24 hours after the horror.
Dr Mark Fowler, 69, came to the door of the house just outside Union City, Tennessee and declined to discuss Pike surviving two syringes of the purportedly lethal injection drug pentobarbital.
’Thank you for coming. I have nothing to say,’ he said from behind the screen door of the four-bedroom property set on 1.5 acres.
Fowler lives 160 miles northwest of the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville where 50-year-old Pike was injected with seven needles on Wednesday night, according to one of her attorneys, Randy Spivey.
She remains alive and is in critical condition at an ‘off-site’ medical facility, which local TV station WSMV has named as Vanderbilt University Medical Center.
Pike's case marks the second botched execution in Tennessee this year - both of which were overseen by Fowler.
Fowler was supervising triple-killer Tony Carruthers' execution in May when the death row inmate survived 90 minutes of failed attempts by the medical team to establish an IV connection for the lethal dose.
A complaint against Fowler, filed by Carruthers’ sister, Dr Tonya Hervey, with the Tennessee Department of Health, claimed that 40 minutes into the execution attempt, the doctor took over the search for vein access and announced he was going to set a central line – a large flexible tube inserted into a chest vein.
Dr Mark Fowler, 69, who oversaw the botched execution of murderer and accused satanist Christa Pike in Tennessee was spotted for the first time at his home on Thursday
Christa Gail Pike, now 50, is alive and in critical condition in the hospital after surviving the botched execution
The tube’s needle was pushed into Carruthers’ chest while he was ‘wide awake and groaned in agony,’ the complaint claims.
Dr Hervey also alleges Fowler was unqualified to place the line because he previously admitted in a deposition that he had not performed the procedure for more than a decade.
According to the claim, Carruthers suffered a stroke as a result of the botched execution, leaving him partially paralyzed.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee later called off the execution and gave a one-year reprieve to Carruthers, 58, who was convicted of the 1984 kidnapping and murders of Frederick Tucker, Marcellos Anderson and Anderson’s mother, Delois.
Fowler could face formal disciplinary charges if the health department finds evidence of a violation in its review.
He has previously refused to comment on the complaint on the accusations. But he told NBC, 'Every attempt was made to minimize the defendant’s discomfort in the case at hand.'
According to his LinkedIn profile, Fowler gained his law degree from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville in 1984 and spent three years as a public defender before retraining as a physician in 1996.
Fowler has worked as an ER physician and a family doctor and is reported to hold several medical directorships.
Fowler came to the door of the house just outside Union City, Tennessee but refused to discuss Pike surviving two syringes of the purportedly lethal injection drug pentobarbital
Fowler lives 160 miles northwest of the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville where 50-year-old Pike survived the bungled execution on Wednesday night
Fowler, who lives in this isolated family home in Union City, is reportedly paid $3,000 to oversee each Tennessee execution
He began as an ER physician at Baptist Memorial Hospital in Covington, Tennessee in 2008. Since November 2012 he has held the role of ‘corporate medical director, director regulatory affairs’ at Interstate Blood Bank, according to his LinkedIn profile.
On Facebook, the doctor describes himself as ‘Right of Center… a writer and avid outdoorsman.’
Fowler also supervised triple-killer Tony Carruthers' execution in May when the death row inmate survived 90 minutes of failed attempts by the medical team to establish an IV connection for the lethal dose
He is reportedly paid $3,000 to oversee each Tennessee execution and was also involved in the controversial execution of Byron Black in August of 2025 – described by the killer’s attorney Kelley Henry as ‘100 percent botched.’
Black reportedly cried out in pain and shouted ‘I can’t do this’ and ‘it hurts so bad’ while repeatedly lifting his head, according to Newsweek. He was declared dead ten minutes later.
Details of Fowler's history of cases have come under renewed scrutiny ever since Pike, who was slated to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years, somehow managed to survive.
President Donald Trump was among those to blast Tennessee officials over the failure to execute her.
'How does that happen?' Trump said on Thursday. 'Should be easy to do. It shouldn't be very difficult.'
Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of her Knoxville Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer, was taken to a hospital on Wednesday night after surviving a double dose of the lethal injection drug
Pike sang, groaned and snored during her more than 90 minutes in the death chamber (pictured) at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution
Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of her Knoxville Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer, was taken to a hospital on Wednesday night after surviving a double dose of the drug Tennessee uses to execute prisoners.
It was not immediately clear what went wrong.
Pike's attorneys said the execution team had worked for an hour to administer the lethal drugs as they struggled to locate a vein.
Spivey, one of her attorneys, said he counted at least seven needles in Pike's left arm.
Pike was singing, cackling and blessing those people in the spectators' room after she had received the first dose that should have killed her, her attorney said.
The scene became even more bizarre when, after the second failed dose, Pike started snoring.
Soon after, witnesses were escorted from the area as Pike was rushed to the hospital, according to her attorney.
More than 24 hours later, Pike's attorneys said she was still in critical condition and receiving 'lifesaving care.'
'We don’t have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment,' Spivey told reporters.
'But we know she is alive right now.'
Pike had been on death row ever since she was convicted over the 1995 murder of her Knoxville Job Corps classmate Colleen Slemmer
The failed execution led Republican Gov. Bill Lee to order a review - calling what happened 'deeply disturbing' and indefinitely postponing Pike’s execution, as well as another one scheduled for later this year.
Meanwhile, Pike's lawyers now want her death sentence to be commuted.
Pike and her boyfriend had both been convicted of the fatal stabbing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer three decades ago.
The killing stoked fears of Satan worship at the time because of a pentagram carved on Slemmer’s body.
Pike, for her part, never disputed that she helped kill Slemmer, but supporters argued her mental illness and allegations of severe sexual abuse should be considered. She was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder shortly after the killing.
'It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,' Pike once said.

articles.title_orig: 2026 World Cup – Baku: Day 2 Finals Live Recap
articles.title_zh: 2026 World Cup – Baku: Day 2 Finals Live Recap
articles.content_orig:
After ripping a time of 45.84 in the prelims of the 100 free, all eyes will be on Cameron McEvoy in tonight's final in Baku. Archive photo via Mickael Malaper/ Malaper Photography
October 02nd, 2026 Asia , Europe , International , News , Swimming World Cup Series
The second night of finals from the 2026 World Cup stop in Baku gets underway one hour earlier today, with 10 events on tap and plenty of superstars in action.
This morning, Cameron McEvoy turned heads with an impressive 45.84 clocking in the men’s 100 free, putting him in pole position to complete the sprint double after winning the 50 last night over Egor Kornev .
McEvoy is using the World Cup stops to test out how his training for the 100 free is working after finding vast success in the 50 over the past three years.
The women’s 200 free will be one race to watch with Siobhan Haughey claiming the top seed this morning after an impressive 50 free swim on Thursday, while the men’s 50 breast looks like one of the marquee races of the session with a star-studded field headlined by Qin Haiyang and Caspar Corbeau .
Yu Yiting put on a dominant display in the timed final of the women’s 400 IM, opening up a massive early lead before comfortably winning gold by nearly four seconds in a time of 4:24.09.
Yu went out like a rocket, turning in 57.51 after the first 100, not too far off world record pace, and then she checked in at 2:04.30 at the halfway mark, more than six seconds clear of the rest of the field.
Her gap slowly shrunk a bit on the back half, but it didn’t matter as Yu finished well clear of the field in a time that puts her just shy of the Chinese Record set by Ye Shiwen in 2012 (4:23.33).
Yu also took down her lifetime best of 4:27.81, set in 2024.
Great Britain’s Abbie Wood was the fastest breaststroker in the pool, solidifying her silver medal position on the third discipline before holding off Chang Mohan on the freestyle leg to touch 2nd in 4:27.95.
Chang and Waka Kobori both made big pushes on the last 25 to inch ahead of Ellen Walshe and placed 3rd and 4th, respectively. Chang won bronze in 4:28.76 ahead of Kobori (4:28.97) and Walshe (4:29.13).
Known more for his freestyle and butterfly prowess, Egor Kornev showed that his pure speed and dynamic underwaters translates over to backstroke as well, winning the men’s 50 back final in record fashion.
Kornev blasted out to the early lead at the halfway mark, flipping in 10.86, just one one-hundredth off world record pace, and then used another blazing-fast underwater to solidify his lead off the wall, powering home to touch in a final time of 22.23.
The performance shatters Isaac Cooper ‘s World Cup record of 22.58, set in 2024, and pulled him within 12 one-hundredths of Kliment Kolesnikov ‘s world record of 22.11 set in 2022.
Kornev’s previous best time stood at 22.44, set last December at the Vladimir Salnikov Cip.
Pieter Coetze and Pavel Samusenko , who tied for silver at the 2025 World Championships in the 50 back, incredibly did the exact same thing here, posting matching times of 22.51 to share the second step on the podium yet again.
For Coetze, he obliterated his own African and South African Record of 22.75, set in 2024. When he tied with Samusenko last summer at Worlds, he also broke the African Record.
Kolesnikov was in the field, placing 4th in 22.99.
Siobhan Haughey picked up her 20th career World Cup gold medal in impressive fashion, winning the women’s 200 freestyle in a time of 1:51.08.
Haughey, the former world record holder in the event with her Asian Record time of 1:50.31, assumed the lead by the 100-meter turn and then pulled away from the field on the third 50 (28.18) before gaining more time coming home (28.55).
She swept the 200 free at all three World Cup stops in 2022, 2023 and 2024, and appears well on her way to doing it again in 2026. Last year, Australia’s Mollie O’Callaghan broke Haughey’s world record and swept the event at all three legs of the series.
American Anna Peplowski had a consistently-split race to win silver in 1:52.48, dipping under her previous best of 1:52.54 from the 2025 World Cup in Westmont, while China’s Fan Yaqi sat back in 5th with 25 meters to go, but charged home to snag bronze in 1:53.07. Her countrymate Yan Tiaoshan (1:53.43) and Great Britain’s Freya Colbert (1:53.59) were 4th and 5th.
After an impressive win in the 100 IM last night, former Indiana Hoosier Luke Barr delivered another exceptional swim tonight in the final of the men’s 200 IM, claiming gold in decisive fashion.
Barr, using the phenomenal underwaters he’s developed racing in yards, blasted out to the lead at the first 25 and never looked back, soaring to a time of 1:51.34.
The swim marks a massive lifetime best for Barr, who had previously been 1:54.10 at the 2025 World Cup stop in Westmont. Barr moved from Indiana to train with Coley Stickels last June.
Italian Alberto Razzetti sat third throughout the entirety of the race, lurking behind Canadian Finlay Knox , but made a big push on the last 25 with a 12.93 split to snag silver in 1:52.41, with Knox securing the bronze in 1:52.57.
Razzetti wasn’t too far off the 1:52.05 he produced last December at the SC European Championships en route to silver. His lifetime best stands at 1:50.88, set at the 2024 SC Worlds where he also won silver.
After going two-for-two with gold medals in the 50 back and 100 IM on Night 1, Marrit Steenbergen picked up right where she left off on Day 2.
The Dutch star looked smooth en route to winning gold in the women’s 100 back in dominant fashion, putting up a time of 55.17 to tie Kira Toussaint ‘s national record set in 2019.
The performance marked the second best time of the day for Steenbergen, who went 57.76 in the prelims to lower her previous PB of 58.76. Coming into the meet, her LC best time was faster, sitting at 58.33 from this past summer.
Taylor Ruck , the top seed out of the prelims in 56.82, had a strong showing to win silver in 56.49, setting her second PB of the day. Her swim in the heats improved on her previous mark of 56.90, set at the 2025 World Cup in Toronto.
Turning around on a quick double, Anna Peplowski snagged the bronze medal in a time of 56.97, steadily moving through the field over the course of the race after turning 5th at the 25.
Abbie Wood , also swimming a double after the 200 IM, took 4th in 57.56.
In an incredibly tight race, Qin Haiyang found the magic over the closing meters of the men’s 50 breaststroke, stealing the gold medal away from Michael Houlie on the last stroke.
Houlie used his patented front-end speed to establish a narrow early lead, turning in 11.63 at the 2025, and then coming home, Qin managed to move up alongside before out-touching him by three one-hundredths of a second at the wall.
Qin clocked 25.67 for the victory, while Houlie was 25.70 for silver. Qin is the Asian Record holder with his time of 25.38 from 2024, while Houlie was one one-hundredth shy of his best time, having been 25.69 at the 2024 SC Worlds. They were the only two men sub-26 this morning, with Qin clocking 25.81 and Houlie going 25.95 in the prelims.
Russia’s Kirill Prigoda was right with Houlie and Qin at the turn, giving him a buffer over the rest of the field as he claimed bronze in a time of 25.88. Dutch teammates Caspar Corbeau (26.08) and Koen de Groot (26.15) rounded out the top five.
After winning one silver and one bronze last night, Roos Vanotterdijk completed the medal set by winning gold tonight in the women’s 50 fly, clocking 24.96 to be the sole woman under 25 seconds.
Vanotterdijk was just over a tenth shy of her lifetime best of 24.84, set en route to winning silver at the 2025 SC European Championships.
Sweden’s Sara Junevik , who was only 25th in this event last year at SC Euros in 25.94, claimed silver in a time of 25.15, topping the Russian duo of Arina Surkova (25.21) and Aleksandra Kuznetsova (25.35), who were 3rd and 4th.
Junevik’s personal best time stands at 25.04, set back in 2022.

articles.title_orig: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.title_zh: Look up: Saturn is at its brightest this weekend
articles.content_orig:
Saturn is at its biggest and brightest as the ringed planet reaches opposition this weekend.
Opposition happens as Earth passes between Saturn and the Sun, bringing the planet to its closest point to Earth for the year, about 784 million miles (1.26 billion km) away. This minimum distance makes Saturn appear brighter than at any other time this year.
Opposition is a great time to observe Saturn because it rises in the east around sunset, reaches its highest point around midnight, and remains visible through dawn. It will appear as a yellowish point of light in the eastern and southeastern sky.
You do not need a telescope to see Saturn, but even a small telescope can reveal the planet's rings and the brightest couple of its 293 moons. While you are spotting Saturn, look a bit higher for a large grouping of four stars astronomers call the Great Square of Pegasus. Up and to the right is the Circlet (ring) of Pisces. These are asterisms, or recognizable patterns within the more official constellations of Pegasus (the winged horse) and Pisces (the fish).
2026's view is very different from last year's when Earth crossed the plane of Saturn’s rings. Though the ring system spans about 175,000 miles, it is, on average, about 30 feet thick, so it effectively disappears when viewed edge-on. Since opposition in 2025, the rings are tilted 7.5 degrees from our perspective, bringing them back into view.
Saturn will be at opposition on Sunday morning at 8:21 a.m., but with clouds expected this weekend, the best views will be tonight, Friday, Oct. 2. The planet will remain an excellent evening target for much of the month.
Saturn’s last opposition occurred Sept. 21, 2025. Saturn reaches opposition every 378 days, or about two weeks later each year, as Earth catches up with Saturn in its orbit. We'll have similar good opportunities to view Jupiter as it reaches its own opposition on Feb. 11, 2027, followed by Mars on Feb. 19, 2027.

articles.title_orig: The world’s 10 most stress-free destinations
articles.title_zh: The world’s 10 most stress-free destinations
articles.content_orig:
Emma is a freelance travel journalist and long-standing contributor to The Telegraph. She is the recipient of several writing awards and has twice been named BGTW Travel Writer of the Year. She has spoken as a travel expert at the Royal Geographical Society, the Frontline Club and National Geographic headquarters in Washington DC and her Scottish lilt can occasionally be heard on the BBC’s From Our Own Correspondent. She can be contacted via Instagram at @emmathomsontravels
Emails. Phone calls. Appointments. Passwords. Protein. Water. Eight hours of sleep. Our lives have become a relentless pursuit of doing – and doing everything better. Even travelling can become a to-do list of bucket-list experiences, country counts and “Instagrammable” moments.
The antidote? The (admittedly laughably named) “stillcation” – a new way of holidaying that pushes back against our culture of constant productivity and self-improvement.
It’s not necessarily yoga at sunrise or a silent meditation retreat, although it can be. More simply, it’s about the absence of agenda. Of stripping life back to its essentials: good food, beautiful views, fresh air and anchoring yourself in the present moment. Instead of seeking destinations that offer the most to do, it asks where offers the best conditions for doing less.
“Man’s inability to sit quietly in a room alone” was, according to French philosopher Blaise Pascal, the source of all humanity’s problems. Four centuries later, his observation feels oddly prescient. We are rarely sitting still – even when on holiday.
The constant pressure to optimise our lives can lead to chronic dysregulation of the nervous system, says Jamie Clements, a wellness retreat facilitator and author of the upcoming book The Next Breath . “Stress has become the baseline, and calm feels like the exception.”
Tour operators are catching onto our increasing thirst for deeper ways to unplug. Inghams recently ranked almost 100 European destinations according to their “stillest”, with criteria including walking trails per square kilometre, air quality, birdsong richness, stargazing quality, human density and forest cover (Scotland’s Wester Ross, see below, took the top spot).
Black Tomato is designing itineraries centred around themes such as “The Gift of Boredom” and “Sonic Sanctuaries”, with quiet-hour museum slots and low-stimulation dining. We’ve also seen a proliferation of Unplugged detox cabins and AirBnbs offering Wi-Fi and technology-free countryside boltholes.
Slowing down switches our nervous system from a fight-or-flight sympathetic state to a rest-and-digest parasympathetic system that lowers blood pressure and improves concentration by possibly stimulating neurogenesis – the creation of new brain cells.
But don’t assume that a stillcation will immediately evoke a state of inward zen. Like any other holiday – where it can take a week to unwind – the first day or two can feel uncomfortable.
The point of a stillcation isn’t simply that sitting around feels nice. Removing the constant demand for attention – and replacing the thrum of traffic, screens and notifications with wind, water, birdsong and walking – may create the conditions in which both mind and body can begin to really recover.
And the benefits extend beyond our own wellbeing. Several of the qualities that make a destination “still” – low population density, dark skies, forests, clean air, biodiversity and quiet trails – are also qualities that depend on healthy, protected environments.
Perhaps that is the real appeal of the stillcation. It doesn’t ask us to abandon movement, curiosity or adventure. It simply changes the objective. Travel becomes less about collecting experiences and more about noticing where we are; less about escaping life and more about inhabiting it. In a culture that has turned even rest into something to optimise, doing nothing might be the most radical itinerary of all.
Lungfuls of salty Cornish coastal air, strolls along the South West Coast Path and its secluded beaches, plus one of the UK’s last remaining temperate rainforests make this the ideal space to slow down.
How to do it: Jamie Clements offers a four-day breathwork retreat at Cabilla in Cornwall from £1,250 per person.
Wester Ross – in the remote north-west highlands of Scotland – is an unspoilt mash of moorlands and mountains that is home to pine martens, otters and the elusive wild cat. Its minimal light pollution creates star-rich dark skies.
How to do it: Wildlife Worldwide offer a six-day The Splendours of Wester Ross tour from £1,295 per person.
Glimpse magic in this Swedish Lapland village that’s probably one of the best places on Earth to see the northern lights (September–April) due to its cloud-free “blue hole”.
How to do it: Arctic Direct offer a three-night Abisko tour from £1,795 per person, including flights and activities.
Creating a wrinkled border between France and Spain, the bird-rich Pyrenees are scarce on people and big on open spaces for mindful hiking, yoga and thermal spas to unwind.
How to do it: Much Better Adventures offer a six-night Hike and Wild Swim in the French Pyrenees tour from £1,688 per person, excluding flights.
Switzerland’s “secret valley” is scattered with lö da ler (wooden cabins with books and reading benches), mindful running trails and forest bathing opportunities, including the Senda Botanica – a narrow path through 30 species of trees.
How to do it: Inntravel offer a seven-night Walking and Wildflowers in the Engadine Valley guided tour from £2,086 per person, excluding flights.
Described as one of the last pristine wilderness areas left on Earth, Yukon has a population of about 48,000 people spread across a territory roughly the size of Spain. It offers an extraordinary sense of space for hiking, wildlife watching, paddling and simply being outdoors.
How to do it: Canadian Sky offer a 10-night In the Footsteps of the Yukon Pioneers self-drive tour from £2,069 per person, including flights.
New Zealand ranks second in the world for peacefulness, behind Iceland. Pick the South Island’s Fiordland, Glenorchy and wild West Coast for vast mountains, sparse settlements and trails where the only itinerary is to walk, breathe and look.
How to do it: Pure Pods has off-grid glass cabins scattered across New Zealand from £240 per night.
Mountain trails, monasteries lit by butter lamps and a deliberately low-volume tourism model make Bhutan in south Asia particularly well suited to a holiday centred on contemplation rather than consumption.
How to do it: Raven Tours offer a nine-day Yoga, Culture and Stillness in the Kingdom of Happiness tour from £2,676 per person based on two sharing.
Nowhere serves up remote stillness quite like Torres del Paine National Park. A raw jostle of glacial lakes, mountains and clear air, it is ideal for forest bathing and restorative walking.
How to do it: Chile Nativo offer a five-day Torres del Paine Wellness Retreat from £1,700 per person from October to April, excluding flights.
One of the world’s least densely populated countries, Namibia in southern Africa is home to the oldest desert in the world, exceptionally dark skies and remarkable wildlife. Don’t miss Sossusvlei, Damaraland and the stark Skeleton Coast.
How to do it: Expert Africa offer a 14-day Discover Namibia self-drive safari from £4,220 per person based on two sharing.

articles.title_orig: How to rule the world: The book review no one asked for
articles.title_zh: How to rule the world: The book review no one asked for
articles.content_orig:
I am not smart enough to rule the world — though, it's important to note that I was planning to. I did not walk into my high school guidance counselor's office, crumple up the state-school brochures, and proclaim I wanted to be a dictator, but I liked having the option. Tragically, this backup plan was crushed when I read Theo Baker’s “How to Rule the World.”
My mother strong-armed this book into my life, proclaiming I would identify with the author.
Like any 19-year-old, I ignored this recommendation, creating a multi-month argument with my parent for no apparent reason. I finally made it around to reading the book between my busy summer schedule of rewatching trashy TV and staring at a wall, only to immediately read that the author I was supposed to be so similar to was a self-described nerd. Thanks, Mom; love you too.
I went into the book with absolutely no context, because I refused to read the jacket as a form of protest. The worst part of the book was… I actually liked it. Not just liked; I loved it to the point I became one of those pretentious people who bring a hard-cover book to appointments, coffee shops, even a tennis match. I was just waiting for someone to ask those magic words, "What are you reading?” What had become of me? The last book I read had watercolor rabbits on the cover. They say drugs are a gateway to a life of disaster; I argue this book set me on a worse track… I was a reader!
You may be asking yourself, “Wow, for a book review I have no clue what this book is actually about.” Well, that's why this article is in the humor section, and why I have not been promoted to culture. I am far too self-centered for ethical journalism. Which, ironically, is what the book is about.
Theo Baker was the student journalist who broke the story that led to Stanford President Marc Tessier-Lavigne's resignation. Baker published “How to Rule the World,” documenting the investigative process that exposed Lavigne's falsified scientific reports and uncovered the toxic symbiotic relationship between Stanford's elite students and Silicon Valley's aggressive venture capitalists.
His investigative journalism earned him the George Polk Award, making him the youngest recipient ever at just 18. I would like to take a moment for that to sink in. He was only a freshman. When I was a freshman, I was just trying to figure out how to do my laundry. I was definitely not cracking the core of our nation's problems with capitalism. I mean, it was on my to-do list, but I just never got around to it.
If, for some reason, you are reading this, Theo Baker, I mean, why wouldn't you be? I'm positive The Miami Student has a national foothold. Just know, the high-achieving STEM parents of the world (my mother) see you as their surrogate successful child when their kid decides to go down the dark path of wanting to be a comedian.
I could go more in-depth on the book's discussion of the intricacies of venture capital in the tech industry and Big Pharma, but I honestly was not smart enough to understand it all and would probably get sued for libel. I will say, to all the young people trying to find their place morally, intellectually, and socially: “How to Rule the World” is an incredibly motivating story urging Gen Z to go past their societal constraints to achieve their goals while striving to create a better, more truthful world. And to President Crawford, don’t worry, I am definitely not clever enough to be an investigative journalist!
Who in the newsroom wants to talk about organic chemistry? Carley would love to.
Mia loves the environment and will do anything to help it flourish. Although, there was this one time...
Cupcake games are awesome... but not for the team that is the cupcake.

articles.title_orig: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.title_zh: NFCB Names Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett Co-Directors
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › People News
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has announced that Serah Mead and Gretchen Aston-Puckett will serve as co-directors starting next year, while Rima Dael will conclude her service as CEO.
Mead, NFCB’s director of member engagement, and Aston-Puckett, its chief operating officer, bring around four decades of combined nonprofit and community media experience, including work at KZMU(FM) in Utah and KVNF(FM) in Colorado.
The change is effective Jan. 1. With the move, Rima Dael will conclude her service as the organization’s CEO at the end of December as the association moves to a two-person permanent staff. The nonprofit has a nine-person board of directors.
[Related: “Future in Focus: Rima Dael of the NFCB”]
Dael supported the structural change and is helping lead the transition, according to NFCB. She has not accepted another position. The organization’s board credited Dael’s leadership in strengthening fundraising, research, partnerships and national advocacy.
According to a release, the change follows board and staff planning in response to the loss of Corporation for Public Broadcasting support. NFCB said it is aligning its expenses with membership revenue while keeping assistance, training, regulatory guidance, resources and peer connections as its focus.
NFCB received a $1.25 million general operating grant from the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation in 2025. It is investing in member resources including rural audience research, an updated legal handbook, emergency preparedness tools and station training.
The National Federation of Community Broadcasters has been serving the nation’s community radio stations since 1978.

articles.title_orig: An Ebola treatment center was burned down as the death toll in Congo passes 4,000 - ABC News
articles.title_zh: An Ebola treatment center was burned down as the death toll in Congo passes 4,000 - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Congo's Ebola outbreak has resulted in over 4,000 deaths, with authorities struggling to contain the virus
BUNIA, Congo -- Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 4,000 people, authorities said, as they struggle to contain what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history .
The latest figures released by the Health Ministry on Thursday showed that 4,018 people have died among 8,300 cases recorded since the outbreak was declared in eastern Congo on May 15.
Some health workers, meanwhile, gathered at the epicenter in Ituri Province to demand payment for wages owed them. The protesters, who included surveillance team members, waved placards saying, “No money, no data!” and “No payment for months.”
Some of the workers haven't been paid for August and September, said Biongi Beiza, one of the protesters in Bunia, Ituri's capital. “There is no explanation from the administration,” he said.
Congolese authorities did not immediately address the issue. Front-line workers have gone on strike several times since the outbreak began, further hampering efforts to contain the disease.
A senior U.N. official said an Ebola-hit displacement camp housing a transit center for infected patients was burned by soldiers earlier this week as they were looking for weapons in Kigonze, on the outskirts of Bunia, forcing 19,000 people in the camp to flee.
Creating such transit and treatment centers has been a struggle, requiring money and staff, all of which are in short supply, said Julien Harneis, the U.N. senior Ebola coordinator. "When we lose a center, that means we lose capacity, we lose investment, and we have to start again. And above all, it means that people do not get access to the care that they really need,” Harneis said.
An aid worker with Médecins Sans Frontières, known in English as Doctors Without Borders, was infected with Ebola while working in Congo, the group said in a statement.
The worker arrived in the Netherlands late Thursday on a special medical flight and was transferred to a high-level isolation unit, the Leiden University Medical Center said in a statement.
“The human cost of this crisis is unprecedented in the DRC, with communities facing the largest Ebola disease outbreak ever recorded in the country,” MSF said.
At least 50 health workers have died after contracting the virus.
One way local authorities have tried to contain the outbreak is through mobile laboratories. In Butembo, an Associated Press journalist watched a medical team operating one such lab near an Ebola treatment center on Thursday.
Test results that used to take 72 hours can now be obtained in six hours with the mobile labs, said Lota Kalubi, a doctor at the treatment center.
The labs have also made it easier to get to locations usually difficult to reach, said Michel Ngimba with the National Institute of Biomedical Research in Butembo. “So we can go, if today we have an emergency, for example, in Katwa, we can start up the vehicle, and we can move the lab to Katwa,” said Ngimba.
The World Health Organization has recently raised the alarm about the virus’ rapid spread into new health zones, stretching limited resources. The current outbreak is on track to exceed the deadliest on record, West Africa’s regional outbreak between 2014 and 2016, which killed 11,000 people, WHO has said.
The number of newly confirmed cases is falling, but that could be attributed to insecurity and challenges in getting communities to cooperate in some of the hot spots, Africa CDC said on Thursday. While the spread of the disease has slowed in some areas, it has accelerated in others.
Confirmed cases fell from around 850 cases and 470 deaths a week in mid-July to an average of 490 cases and 230 deaths in September.
A Congolese politician was beaten to death earlier this week in one of the emerging hot spots after defending government measures to deal with the outbreak, highlighting tensions and mistrust in communities.
Authorities last month launched a village-centered approach that involved working with local leaders to educate people about the virus, but those efforts face resistance from residents who dismiss Ebola as a hoax. There is also deep distrust in the country’s government for reasons including how it’s managed past Ebola outbreaks and chronic corruption.
Adetayo reported from Lagos, Nigeria. Sebastien Kitsa Musayi in Butembo, Congo, Chinedu Asadu in Abuja, Nigeria, and Mike Corder in the Netherlands contributed.
For more on Africa and development: https://apnews.com/hub/africa-pulse

articles.title_orig: Officials Say NVIDIA Missed Red Flags in China Chip Smuggling Cases
articles.title_zh: Officials Say NVIDIA Missed Red Flags in China Chip Smuggling Cases
articles.content_orig:
Federal prosecutors have charged a man with illegally shipping NVIDIA artificial intelligence chips to China, Bloomberg reported on Oct. 2.
Government officials told Bloomberg in a feature published Oct. 1 that NVIDIA is not doing enough to stop the trade. NVIDIA has never been accused of helping smugglers. It says it has followed the rules.
The Justice Department announced the arrest of Greg Lui on Oct. 1. He is accused of smuggling servers holding $300 million worth of AI chips to China in violation of US export laws.
Earlier this year, officials released surveillance video. It shows a person using a red hair dryer to peel serial number stickers off NVIDIA server boxes.
Bloomberg cited one warning sign. Thailand and Singapore, both next to China, were receiving more chips than they could use. Daniel Remler, a former State Department AI policy head, said he never received a straight answer.
His question was how so many chips could flow to Southeast Asia if they were not serving Chinese customers.
Bloomberg also reported that operators in western China were building dozens of data centers able to house 115,000 restricted NVIDIA processors. Its sources said US officials now believe China has smuggled at least that many chips.
The accused collaborators in one case include Yih-Shyan Liaw, a co-founder of Super Micro. They allegedly sold about $2.5 billion worth of AI servers to OBON, a Bangkok-based company that was supposedly building AI infrastructure in Thailand.
Instead, the servers went straight to end users in China. To get past compliance officers, the conspirators allegedly peeled stickers from genuine NVIDIA products with a hair dryer and attached them to dummy servers.
Officials told Bloomberg that NVIDIA should have noticed OBON lacked the 100 megawatts of data center space needed to host that many servers. Thailand has only a few hundred megawatts of AI data center capacity running. Such a build would have drawn attention.
NVIDIA disputes that view. A spokesperson said a startup's growth plan in a friendly country is an opportunity for America, not a red flag.
The spokesperson said NVIDIA-powered servers are financeable assets that help startups secure capital and infrastructure, including data center space. American companies, the spokesperson added, honor US laws as written.
The company also said progress by Huawei in AI chips means Chinese buyers have no need to smuggle in NVIDIA hardware.
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has lobbied US officials to ease export curbs on China and other Asian nations. Last year, the Trump administration agreed to allow sales of NVIDIA's previous-generation Hopper H200 accelerators to China.
I cover what the internet is actually talking about: the new release, the viral moment, the creator beef, the product launch. My job is to explain it fast and clearly, without the breathless hype. I read the timeline…

articles.title_orig: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named to TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars List
articles.title_zh: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Named to TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars List
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) this week was named to the TIME100 Next 2026: The World’s Most Influential Rising Stars list. Senator Britt is the only Republican lawmaker and the only Alabamian named to this year’s list. She is just the second Alabamian ever to receive the honor.
The announcement from TIME can be read below:
“Senator Katie Britt has quickly learned how to wield influence in Donald Trump’s Republican Party while avoiding its hardest edges.
“Not long after she became in 2022 the youngest Republican woman ever elected to the Senate, Mitch McConnell invited her to join his weekly leadership meetings as an adviser, giving her access to the GOP’s longtime power center.
“Britt, 44, has since strongly backed Trump’s agenda, including his aggressive immigration policies, while privately urging the Administration toward moderation at key moments.
“The Alabama lawmaker has also carved out her own policy lane around families and children. Britt pressed Trump to protect IVF after an Alabama court ruling threatened access to the procedure, helped secure expanded childcare tax credits, and has worked across the aisle on legislation protecting children from social media. Her ability to bridge divides within the GOP while cultivating bipartisan relationships has made Britt an increasingly consequential player in the Senate.”
Senator Britt released the following statement in response to the honor:
“I’m deeply humbled by this recognition, but it truly belongs to the people of Alabama. Every single day, I’m focused on making sure the hardworking families in our state and across our nation have the opportunity to thrive — whether that’s making childcare more affordable and accessible, ensuring continued nationwide access to IVF, keeping our nation safe and secure, or protecting our kids online. Serving Alabama is the honor of a lifetime, and I’ll keep fighting day in and day out to put the people I represent in a stronger place as a result of my service.”

articles.title_orig: Looking to expand in China? iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 connects global suppliers with Chinese buyers
articles.title_zh: Looking to expand in China? iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 connects global suppliers with Chinese buyers
articles.content_orig:
The 19th iFresh Asia Fruit Expo will take place from November 4–6, 2026, at Hangzhou International Expo Center Phase II in Hangzhou, China, bringing together more than 500 exhibitors and 8,000 professional visitors across the fresh produce value chain.
For international fruit companies looking to enter or expand in China, finding an importer is only the beginning.
China has a large and rapidly evolving fresh produce market, with channels ranging from wholesale markets, fruit retail chains and supermarkets to e-commerce platforms, premium fruit stores and emerging retail formats. Each channel has different requirements when it comes to varieties, quality, specifications, packaging, pricing, and supply consistency.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
Which products are Chinese buyers looking for? Which channels offer new opportunities for imported fruit? How can international suppliers find the right partners? And what trends are shaping China’s fruit market today?
These are some of the questions that international companies will have the opportunity to explore at iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 , taking place from November 4–6 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China .
For companies seeking more Chinese buyers, new distribution channels, reliable local partners, and a better understanding of the latest developments in China’s fruit market , Hangzhou will provide three days of concentrated access to the industry.
The 2026 edition of iFresh Asia Fruit Expo will cover approximately 20,000 square meters , bringing together 500+ exhibitors and 8,000 professional visitors .
The exhibition spans the fruit industry value chain, from seedlings, fresh produce, and fruit brands to processed fruit products, post-harvest technology, preservation, sorting, packaging, and cold-chain logistics.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
Six dedicated exhibition areas will showcase different segments of the industry:
Fresh Fruit & Brand Zone | International Fruit Zone | Technology & Supply Chain Zone | Fruit Processing Zone | Fruit Channel Food Zone | Organic Food Brand Zone
For international suppliers, participating in iFresh is not simply about displaying products. It is an opportunity to meet potential partners from different parts of China’s fruit distribution and supply chain ecosystem in one place.
Whether a company wants to introduce fresh fruit to China, identify importers and distributors, explore new retail channels, or discover solutions in preservation, sorting, packaging, and cold-chain logistics, the expo is designed to provide direct access to relevant industry resources.
For B2B exhibitors, the number of contacts collected at a trade show matters less than whether those contacts lead to real business opportunities.
That is why business matchmaking will be a major focus of this year’s iFresh Asia Fruit Expo.
Hangzhou is widely recognized as one of China’s leading e-commerce hubs and is located in the Yangtze River Delta, one of the country’s most economically active consumer markets.
Against this backdrop, the expo will bring together professional buyers and decision-makers from wholesale markets, fruit retail chains, supermarkets, e-commerce platforms, new retail businesses, supply chain companies, and other distribution channels .
Dedicated Fresh Fruit & Fruit Channel Food Business Matchmaking Sessions will also take place during the exhibition, alongside the “100 Counties, 100 Products” Roadshow & Matchmaking Program .
These activities are designed to bring suppliers closer to buyers with actual sourcing needs, creating more focused opportunities for face-to-face business discussions.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
For companies entering China for the first time, this is also an opportunity to hear directly from Chinese buyers about what they are looking for — from product quality and specifications to packaging, pricing, and supply requirements.
For international brands and suppliers already active in China, the iFresh Asia Fruit Expo offers a chance to explore additional channels, regional markets and potential new partners.
One new feature of this year’s exhibition is the dedicated Fruit Channel Food Zone , reflecting changes taking place across China’s fruit retail sector.
A growing number of fruit retailers in China are expanding beyond fresh produce and introducing products such as dried fruit, fruit snacks, juices and other complementary food categories.
For retailers, these products can help broaden their product mix, extend shelf life, create more consumption occasions and generate additional revenue beyond fresh fruit sales.
For international suppliers, this means opportunities within China’s fruit retail channels are no longer limited to fresh produce.
Global fruit processors, snack brands and food companies with products suitable for fruit retail environments can also use the expo to connect with Chinese fruit chains, retailers, distributors and professional buyers.
Entering a market is not only about finding customers. It is also about understanding where the market is heading.
Alongside the exhibition, iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 will host a series of industry conferences under the Fruit Elite Island program, covering key topics currently being discussed across China’s fruit industry.
The conference program includes:
The sessions will bring together industry professionals and business representatives to discuss developments across fruit growing, retail, branding, wholesale and distribution, processing, organic food and emerging business models .
For international companies, the value goes beyond attending a conference.
Companies that want to build a long-term presence in China need to understand what Chinese buyers are discussing, how distribution channels are changing, what retailers are looking for, and where new consumer and product opportunities are emerging .
Through three days of exhibitions, matchmaking, and industry discussions, overseas participants can gain a closer look at the dynamics shaping China’s fruit business.
China offers significant opportunities, but building a sustainable business in the market requires more than simply bringing a product into the country.
Finding the right buyers, understanding channel requirements, developing local partnerships, and keeping pace with market changes are all essential.
Image by iFresh Asia Fruit Expo
If you are looking for more Chinese buyers, if you want to expand your distribution network in China, if you are searching for importers, distributors or long-term business partners, or if you want a closer look at the latest trends shaping China’s fruit market,
iFresh Asia Fruit Expo 2026 is an opportunity to connect with the market face-to-face.
From product showcases and targeted buyer matchmaking to industry insights and full supply-chain connections, the three-day event aims to create practical business opportunities between international suppliers and China’s fruit industry.

articles.content_orig:
The FIFA Council will hear an update on the bid process for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which is tentatively slated to be held in the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, at its Oct. 14 meeting. It will be the first such update since FIFA delayed the vote on awarding the event to the four nations from its Congress this past April to an Extraordinary Congress on Nov. 23.
The joint bid from the four Concacaf nations , submitted last November, is the only one for the 2031 Women’s World Cup. It included 35 prospective host cities: 27 in the U.S., six in Mexico and one each in Jamaica and Costa Rica.
Because of the one-sided nature of the host city agreements for the 2026 men’s World Cup, however, the prospective U.S. host cities refused to agree to specific hosting terms before the 2031 bid was submitted. They are seeking an opportunity to negotiate more favorable terms that would reduce their financial and operational burdens while providing greater revenue opportunities.
It is unknown whether any meaningful discussions have taken place since the conclusion of the men’s World Cup regarding new terms for the 2031 Women’s World Cup. U.S. Soccer is expected to play a role in facilitating those discussions after largely being sidelined in the delivery of the men’s World Cup.
The Women’s World Cup bidding update will also touch on the 2035 Women’s World Cup, for which the U.K. is the lone bidder. Other notable agenda items for the Oct. 14 meeting include a review of President Gianni Infantino’s controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise investment proposal, which was scrapped following massive backlash , as well as reviews of FIFA’s reserves and the financing of its member associations. The agenda also mentions a discussion of the FIFA Peace Prize, which was awarded for the first time in 2025 to President Trump .
The FIFA Council has 37 members, including representatives elected through each of the six regional confederations. U.S. Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone sits on the council as Concacaf’s North American representative.

articles.title_orig: 5 European nations follow U.S. with plans for third-country deportations as EU approves migrant "return hubs"
articles.title_zh: 5 European nations follow U.S. with plans for third-country deportations as EU approves migrant "return hubs"
articles.content_orig:
Five European Union countries are pushing ahead with plans to start deporting asylum seekers whose applications are rejected to third countries outside the bloc, potentially in Africa, after the EU approved new rules this week that clear the way for the practice.
Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands have agreed on a common framework to establish "return hubs" outside the EU to which people who have exhausted their legal options to remain in Europe could be transferred if they cannot be sent back to their own countries of origin.
"When it comes to return hubs, it's progressing very well," Danish Interior Minister Morten Bødskov told reporters Thursday, according to AFP . "We are moving in the right direction."
He previously said Denmark expected "to be ready to transfer the first irregular migrants to a partner country outside the EU within 2027."
Greek Migration Minister Thanos Plevris told Politico that Greece expects to have a pilot project in place in the first half of next year.
No potential destinations for EU return hubs have been confirmed, although Rwanda has been reported as a possible partner in the project. A Greek government statement on the plans said the hubs would be established in safe third countries, "particularly on the African continent."
The EU itself has presented the idea of return hubs as a potential deterrent to irregular immigration. A discussion paper published by the EU's governing European Council in October 2025 said the hubs could "incentivize voluntary returns," because migrants who fail to comply with a deportation order could face transfer to a hub instead.
It said the policy could also discourage people without a valid asylum claim from making dangerous journeys to Europe.
The rules adopted this week by the EU establish a bloc-wide legal framework for returns and allow member states to conclude bilateral or unilateral agreements with countries outside the bloc, but with stipulations.
Under the rules, "any such agreement or arrangement may only be concluded with a non-EU country that respects international human rights standards and principles of international law, including the principle of non-refoulement ," which guarantees that no individual can be sent back to a country where they would face torture, cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, punishment or other irreparable harm.
The Trump administration has enthusiastically embraced the use of third-country deportations to remove undocumented migrants from the United States. More than 100 deportees were sent to eight African countries over a 10-day period in August, according to internal U.S. government documents obtained by CBS News .
The deportees were sent to destinations including the African nations of Liberia, Rwanda, Eswatini and Sierra Leone.
Plevris, Greece's migration minister, has praised the Trump administration's approach.
"I am a fan of President Trump," he told Breitbart in August. "But if you ask me what was the best thing he did, it was change the migration policy of the USA, because now we have a new migration policy also in Europe."
Other European governments have experimented with deportations to third nations before, however, with mixed results.
Britain's former Conservative Party government sought to send asylum seekers who arrived through irregular routes to Rwanda to have their claims processed there. The U.K. Supreme Court ruled the scheme unlawful in 2023, before it ever got going, over the risk that refugees could ultimately be returned to countries where they faced persecution.
The following year, the policy was formally abandoned by the new Labour Party government after the Conservatives were voted out of power. The British Home Office said £715 million (almost $950 million) had been spent on the Rwanda program by June 2024, and no asylum seekers were forcibly relocated. Four people traveled voluntarily to Rwanda under the program.
"One lesson may be that European governments should expect litigation, even where the third country looks considerably less controversial than Rwanda," Peter Walsh, a senior researcher at the University of Oxford's Migration Observatory, told CBS News on Friday.
"These policies are often justified as deterrence measures, and that assumes a sufficiently large share of people believe there is a realistic chance they will actually be transferred," Walsh said. "If only a very small proportion can be moved, the deterrent may be much less credible."
"The broader lesson from Rwanda is that externalization is not a shortcut around the difficult parts of migration policy," he said. "It may relocate some of those difficulties geographically, but governments still have to deal with courts, individual rights, administrative capacity, countries that may not cooperate with returns, and substantial costs"
The push for return hubs is part of a broader effort by European nations to tighten their immigration policies amid intense pressure on governments to increase the number of people without a legal right to remain who are actually removed.
Jacob Reynolds, policy director at the Freedom and Sovereignty Initiative Europe, a right-wing think tank based in Brussels, called the EU decision to embrace these hubs a "welcome step towards gaining control of our borders and removing those who have no right to be here."
But he added that "outsourcing the problem of illegal migration to third countries — as the EU has long done — risks avoiding the broader problem: the lack of control over EU countries' borders."
He called for "much more fundamental action" to address "the generous regimes available to asylum seekers in Europe," and said until that happened, "the problem will not be solved."

articles.title_orig: Funding Shortages Threaten World Heritage Sites
articles.title_zh: Funding Shortages Threaten World Heritage Sites
articles.content_orig:
By providing your information, you agree to our Terms of Use and our Privacy Policy .
				We use vendors that may also process your information to help provide our services.
The World Monuments Fund (WMF), an independent organization, has warned that funding constraints, intensifying climate change, and a lack of access to expertise are putting World Heritage Sites at extreme risk.
The information comes from WMF’s review of 372 nominations submitted by the public from around the globe as research for the upcoming biannual World Monuments Watch (WMW) list, which will be announced in February. According to the findings, eighty-six percent of nominators cited “funding shortages and economic development” as a primary issue, an increase of 6 percent from last year. Simultaneously, 63 percent identified “opportunities to leverage heritage to support local economies through sustainable tourism, job creation, and urban regeneration.”
“This year’s nominations show that the pressures on heritage are intensifying while the resources to protect it are not keeping pace,” Bénédicte de Montlaur, WMF president and CEO, said in a press release. “According to findings in the UNESCO Global Report on Cultural Policies, only one in four countries has the means to safeguard its heritage.”
Sixty-six percent of nominators cited climate hazards as another major concern, and 30 percent said sites were directly threatened by extreme weather events, flooding, storms, drought, and wildfires. Climate impacts are most severe in sub-Saharan Africa, where 86 percent of sites are under threat. At the same time, the need for technical expertise is increasing, yet 35 percent of nominators identified a “severe lack” of local preservation expertise. In Ghana, for instance, the ten shrines of the Asante Traditional Buildings are endangered as traditional stewardship by master craftspeople declines.
Brinda Somaya, an architect and chair of the WMW International Expert Panel, emphasized the urgency of addressing these risks. “Protecting these sites is vital for preserving local memory, fostering economic resilience, and supporting the communities tied to these places,” she said.
